items.name: Water
items.quantity: One gallon per person per day for several days, for drinking and sanitation (Ready.gov). Bottled water for 3 days: 3 litres per person per day for drinking, more for cooking and washing (Be Ready).
items.why: After an emergency, you may need to survive on your own for several days (Ready.gov).

items.name: Non-perishable food
items.quantity: At least a several-day supply of non-perishable food (Ready.gov). Non-perishable food for 3 days that doesn't need refrigeration or cooking, such as tinned meat, fish or vegetables, dried fruit and nuts (Be Ready).
items.why: Be Ready says it is best to buy long-life food you would usually eat.

items.name: Battery or hand-crank radio
items.quantity: Battery-powered or hand crank radio and a NOAA Weather Radio with tone alert (Ready.gov). FM radio, battery or wind up (Be Ready).
items.why: For updates during outages; Be Ready suggests writing down the frequencies of stations you use for news.

items.name: Flashlight or torch
items.quantity: Flashlight (Ready.gov). Torch (Be Ready).
items.why: Torches are safer than candles (Be Ready).

items.name: Spare batteries
items.quantity: Extra batteries (Ready.gov). Spare batteries for the torch (Be Ready).
items.why: Both lists pair spare batteries with the light and radio so they keep working during an outage.

items.name: First aid kit
items.quantity: First aid kit (Ready.gov). First aid kit or items such as waterproof plasters, bandages, a thermometer, antiseptic, eyewash solution, sterile dressings, gloves, medical tape and tweezers (Be Ready).
items.why: Both lists treat basic first aid supplies as part of the core kit.

items.name: Phone charger and power bank
items.quantity: Cell phone with chargers and a backup battery (Ready.gov). Charged power bank (Be Ready).
items.why: To charge phones or compatible medical devices (Be Ready).

items.name: Medications and eyeglasses
items.quantity: Prescription medications; non-prescription medications such as pain relievers, anti-diarrhea medication, antacids or laxatives; prescription eyeglasses and contact lens solution (Ready.gov). Essential medication and medical supplies (Be Ready).
items.why: An emergency can make it difficult to refill a prescription or find an open pharmacy (Ready.gov); Be Ready advises requesting repeats up to 5 working days ahead.
items.amazonQuery: weekly pill organizer travel medicine case

items.name: Hygiene and sanitation supplies
items.quantity: Moist towelettes, garbage bags and plastic ties for personal sanitation; soap, hand sanitizer and disinfecting wipes; feminine supplies and personal hygiene items (Ready.gov). Hand sanitiser, wet wipes and bathroom products (Be Ready).
items.why: Ready.gov lists these for personal sanitation when water and services are disrupted.
items.amazonQuery: emergency hygiene kit wet wipes hand sanitizer

items.name: Blankets and warm clothing
items.quantity: Sleeping bag or warm blanket for each person; complete change of clothing appropriate for your climate and sturdy shoes (Ready.gov). Blankets, sleeping bags and warm clothing (Be Ready).
items.why: Homes can become cold very quickly when the heating goes off (Be Ready).

items.name: Cash
items.quantity: Cash or traveler's checks (Ready.gov). Cash, a mix of coins and notes, and cards (Be Ready).
items.why: In case electronic payments or ATMs are disrupted (Be Ready).

items.name: Copies of important documents
items.quantity: Important family documents such as copies of insurance policies, identification and bank account records saved electronically or in a waterproof, portable container (Ready.gov). Printed copies of IDs and documents such as passports, birth certificates and insurance policy details (Be Ready).
items.why: Both lists say to keep copies you can reach without power or internet.

items.name: Pet food and water
items.quantity: Pet food and extra water for your pet (Ready.gov). Pet food and bottled water (Be Ready).
items.why: Both lists include pets in the household's supply plan.

items.name: Baby supplies
items.quantity: Infant formula, bottles, diapers, wipes and diaper rash cream (Ready.gov). Baby formula, nappies and wipes (Be Ready).
items.why: Ready-made formula is best as you may not be able to boil water to make up powdered formula safely (Be Ready).

items.name: Whistle
items.quantity: Whistle (Ready.gov).
items.why: To signal for help (Ready.gov).

items.name: Dust mask
items.quantity: Dust mask (Ready.gov).
items.why: To help filter contaminated air (Ready.gov).

items.name: Plastic sheeting, scissors and duct tape
items.quantity: Plastic sheeting, scissors and duct tape (Ready.gov).
items.why: To shelter in place (Ready.gov).

items.name: Wrench or pliers
items.quantity: Wrench or pliers (Ready.gov).
items.why: To turn off utilities (Ready.gov).

items.name: Manual can opener
items.quantity: Manual can opener (Ready.gov).
items.why: For food (Ready.gov).

items.name: Local maps
items.quantity: Local maps (Ready.gov).
items.why: Ready.gov lists paper maps in the basic kit for when phones and navigation are down.

items.name: Written contacts and notes
items.quantity: Important phone numbers and information, including a list of regular medication and doses (Be Ready). Paper and pencil (Ready.gov).
items.why: Be Ready says to write down contact details of who you would need to reach in an emergency.

items.name: Fire extinguisher
items.quantity: Fire extinguisher (Ready.gov).
items.why: Listed by Ready.gov among additional emergency supplies.

items.name: Matches in a waterproof container
items.quantity: Matches in a waterproof container (Ready.gov).
items.why: Listed by Ready.gov among additional emergency supplies.

items.name: Plates, cups and utensils
items.quantity: Mess kits, paper cups, plates, paper towels and plastic utensils (Ready.gov).
items.why: Listed by Ready.gov among additional emergency supplies.

items.name: Activities for children
items.quantity: Books, games, puzzles or other activities for children (Ready.gov).
items.why: Listed by Ready.gov among additional emergency supplies.
